hero.h1: Forex market hours, live in your timezone
hero.definition: Forex market hours are the times each major currency market is open for trading. The forex market runs 24 hours a day, five days a week, across four sessions — Sydney, Tokyo, London and New York — and is closed on weekends. This live clock shows which sessions are open right now in your timezone.

how.h2: How to read the forex market hours clock
how.intro: No sign-up, no downloads needed — just open the page and read the live market hours in three steps.

steps.title: Set your timezone
steps.body: The timeline opens in your local timezone automatically. Switch it to compare any market from anywhere in the world.

steps.title: Read the open markets
steps.body: Each coloured bar is a session's trading window. The moving line is now — wherever it crosses a bar, that market is open.

steps.title: Plan around the overlaps
steps.body: Spot the London–New York overlap and other high-liquidity windows at a glance, then time your trading around them.

sessions.intro: The forex market runs 24 hours a day across the major sessions below. These are the standard windows in GMT; the tool above adjusts them to your timezone and for daylight saving automatically.
sessions.caption: Major forex trading sessions and their approximate opening hours in GMT.

notes.Sydney: Opens the trading week; sets early AUD and NZD tone.
notes.Tokyo: The Asian session; most active for JPY pairs.
notes.Frankfurt: Opens Europe an hour before London; key for EUR pairs.
notes.London: The largest forex session by volume worldwide.
notes.New York: Drives USD volatility; overlaps London mid-afternoon.

sessions.overlapBody: When London and New York are open together, the two largest markets trade at once — typically the deepest liquidity and sharpest moves of the day.
sessions.diagramAlt: Timeline diagram of the Sydney, Tokyo, Frankfurt, London and New York forex sessions across a 24-hour GMT day, with the London–New York overlap highlighted.
sessions.diagramCaption: The five major forex sessions across a 24-hour GMT day. The shaded band marks the London–New York overlap (≈13:00–17:00 GMT), the day's highest-liquidity window.
sessions.statTurnover: For scale: global average daily forex turnover reached $7.5 trillion in April 2022, with UK (London) desks handling the largest share worldwide, according to the Bank for International Settlements' <link>Triennial Central Bank Survey</link>.
sessions.statIana: Every hour on this page is computed live from the <link>IANA Time Zone Database</link> — the timezone reference built into virtually every browser and operating system — so daylight-saving shifts are always accurate.
sessions.relatedReading: Want more detail? Read about the <bestTime>best time to trade forex by session</bestTime>, dig into the <overlap>London–New York overlap</overlap>, or see <methodology>how we calculate these times</methodology>.
sessions.dstNote: Session windows are provided for general information and shift with daylight-saving time (for example, London observes GMT in winter and BST in summer). The app always reflects the current, correctly-adjusted times.

faq.h2: Forex market hours: frequently asked questions

items.a: Yes. The Forex Market Hours web tool is completely free, with no ads and no sign-up. The companion iOS and Android apps are free too.

items.q: Do I need to create an account?
items.a: No account is required. Open the page and the live market hours appear instantly in your timezone.

items.q: Does it give trading signals or financial advice?
items.a: No. It is a market-hours tool that shows when sessions open and close. It does not provide financial advice, trading signals, or any trading, deposit or withdrawal services.

items.q: Which forex sessions does it show?
items.a: The major sessions — Sydney, Tokyo, Frankfurt, London and New York — plus the high-volume session overlaps where volatility tends to peak.

items.q: Are the times correct for daylight saving?
items.a: Yes. Every market's hours are computed from its own timezone rules, so daylight-saving shifts (GMT/BST, EST/EDT, and so on) are always applied automatically.

Yes. Forex Market Hours is available on the App Store (iPhone, iPad, Mac, Apple Vision Pro) and on Google Play for Android, adding widgets, an economic calendar and alerts 15 minutes before each session opens.

items.q: What time does the forex market open and close?
items.a: The forex market opens Sunday at 5:00 PM New York time (22:00 GMT) when Sydney begins trading, and closes Friday at 5:00 PM New York time. It runs 24 hours a day, five days a week, and is closed on weekends.

items.q: Is the forex market open right now?
items.a: The forex market is open 24 hours from Sunday 5 PM ET to Friday 5 PM ET. To see whether a specific session — Sydney, Tokyo, London or New York — is trading at this moment in your timezone, check the live clock at the top of this page.

items.q: What is the best time to trade forex?
items.a: The most active window is the London–New York overlap, roughly 13:00–17:00 GMT, when the two largest markets trade at once. Liquidity is deepest and spreads are tightest then, though volatility is higher. The best time also depends on the currency pairs you trade.

items.q: Why is the London session the most important?
items.a: London is the largest forex trading centre by volume — the UK handles the biggest share of global FX turnover (BIS Triennial Survey). The London open often sets the day's direction, and its afternoon overlaps with New York, creating the busiest hours of the day.

items.q: What are the forex market hours in my timezone?
items.a: Session times are usually quoted in GMT, but this tool converts every session to your local timezone automatically and adjusts for daylight saving — so you see the exact hour each market opens and closes on your own clock, with no manual conversion.
